title: Liam Rosenior feels ‘100 per cent’ support from Chelsea hierarchy despite plummeting form
content:
Chelsea head coach Liam Rosenior insists he feels the “100 per cent” backing from the club’s hierarchy despite the team winning just one of their last eight league games.

Chelsea’s hopes of qualifying for the Champions League via a top five finish are looking increasingly precarious having fallen 10 and seven points behind Aston Villa (fourth) and Liverpool (fifth) respectively, with five league games to go.

The club’s fans have started to turn on Chelsea’s head coach during and after games but Rosenior, who signed a six-and-a-half year contract when he replaced Enzo Maresca in January, is not worried about his future at Stamford Bridge.

When asked if he is feeling the support from the owners, Rosenior replied: “100 per cent. They’ve been supportive of me in our daily conversations, sporting directors involved, they’ve been magnificent in their support of me and the team.

“I don’t think it’s (the conversations they have been having) about needing reassurance. It’s about being open. It’s about seeing where I’ve made mistakes, where we’ve made mistakes, where we need to improve. Having open, honest, challenging conversations makes the process better because if you’re not honest and you don’t hold your hand up to mistakes, you’re never going to improve. I have made mistakes.

“They’ve supported me in many different areas in many different ways and I feel the players understand that we’re all very aligned in terms of what we want to achieve.”

Rosenior revealed that defender Wesley Fofana apologised for his reaction to being substituted in the 1-0 defeat to Manchester United on Saturday.

Fofana ignored Rosenior and barged past assistant Justin Walker, gesturing angrily as he did so. But the centre back will still be considered for selection against Brighton & Hove Albion tomorrow.

Rosenior added: “Wes is a very emotional character in a good way. I love him. As a guy, he’s not afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve. I’ve spoken to him about it and he’s just disappointed that we’re losing the game. I do think he could have shown that emotion in a better way and that’s something that I’ve spoken about but the optics on that is not the reality.

“Wes apologised for his reaction but these are young players who are going to make mistakes in the moment.”

Chelsea will make a late decision on whether Joao Pedro can return from a minor thigh injury to play against his former club. Estevao Willian has been ruled out with a hamstring strain picked up in the United defeat and is still having scans to determine how long he will be out for.
